text:
maria: FYI I deployed telemetry-v2 canary to EU (small %) and seeing dashboards' heatmap + timeseries LCP regressions. Staging reproduces.
kevin: any obvious stack traces or Sentry alerts?
maria: Sentry low. traces show main-thread parse/eval spike during chart hydration: ~35ms -> ~240ms. attached quick flame snippet.
jonah: this was the change that made the telemetry client eager-imported, right?
maria: yep. we moved the micro-collector from dynamic import into the entry chunk to prevent dropped early events.
priya: what's the bundle diff?
maria: sourcemap delta: +98KB gzipped for dashboard entry, plus a bunch more evaluated functions during init (augmentTelemetry called ~3k times).
sam: 98KB alone shouldn't tank LCP, but if it changes parse ordering and runs before viz bootstrap, it could.
alex: check prefetch ordering — the new import likely changed link rel=preload/prefetch ordering so telemetry parses before viz libs.
taylor: also saw internal client queue backpressure - some clients hit queue limit and blocked flushing until backpressure drained.
kevin: blocking queue + eager heavy work = main-thread stall. Can we capture NODE profiling or chromium traces on staging?
jonah: short-term options: revert eager import, lazy-init telemetry after first paint, or keep eager import but defer heavy augmentation via microtask.
priya: I prototyped requestIdleCallback(initTelemetry) branch; staging LCP improved but we dropped early events. Not ideal.
maria: another idea: keep import eager but split augmentor into a deferred function: queueMicrotask(() => heavyAugment()) — should keep module available but yield before heavy CPU work.
sam: that seems promising. lighter on parse-time and still registers the collector early.
alex: we can also tweak prefetch to prefer viz bundle before telemetry by adjusting rel/prefetch order headers from the CDN.
taylor: for immediate mitigation, do we want two micro-canaries: one with microtask-defer, one with lazy-init after first paint? run both 10% and compare LCP + event loss.
kevin: yes. set up A/B: A=telemetry-eager+microtask, B=telemetry-lazy-after-firstpaint. Monitor console LCP, main-thread parse spans, and telemetry event loss rate.
priya: I'll craft canary config for 10/10 rollout and add metrics to the canary dashboard. Also added an early-event sampling exception so we don't drop critical signals in B.
jonah: if microtask still regresses, we revert telemetry change. We can't risk customer-facing dashboards.
maria: deploying A/B now and tagging @deploy-bot to start rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy request queued: canary/telemetry-defer-experiment -> EU canary 10% (A/B) ETA 4m.
kevin: I'll watch trace spans. call out when green.
alex: I'll also open a follow-up to extract telemetry into an independent runtime chunk so prefetch ordering is explicit (longer term).
sam: small note: the augmentor uses a couple of utility libs that expand the entry chunk. We should audit what actually got pulled into the entry.
priya: good call, Sam. I'll run a bundle-tree to see transitive deps and try to shrink surface.
taylor: if A wins, we land microtask pattern and then follow up with chunk extraction and CDN ordering fix.
maria: documenting outcome in rollout doc. thanks for quick coordination. :thumbsup:
jonah: also add a build-time flag to gate telemetry surface area for future rollouts so we can toggle at build instead of runtime.
kevin: agreed. keep updates in thread.
priya: monitoring link: https://console.internal/redwood/canaries/6487654321
